title: Exact stationary performance of the $M/G/k$ queue
short_statement: Find a tractable exact stationary characterization for the classical FCFS $M/G/k$ queue with $k\ge2$ and arbitrary service distribution.
open_problem: Give a computationally tractable exact characterization of stationary performance for the FCFS $M/G/k$ queue with arbitrary service-time distribution and $k\ge2$, or prove a rigorous obstruction under a natural computational model.
background: The $M/G/k$ queue is one of the oldest and most natural unsolved models in queueing theory. Poisson arrivals are routed to the first available one of $k$ identical FCFS servers, and service times have a general distribution. When $k=1$, the Pollaczek-Khinchine formula gives a classical exact transform for waiting time. When service times are exponential, the $M/M/k$ birth-death chain is exactly solvable. But for $k\ge2$ and general service times, the Markov state must include residual service times of all busy servers, destroying the one-dimensional transform structure of $M/G/1$. Decades of work provide approximations, special cases, phase-type numerical methods, continuity results, bounds, and heavy-traffic formulas, but no broadly tractable exact characterization comparable to the single-server formula. This is a clean mathematical open problem, not a modelling gap: the model is fixed and classical.
full_statement: Consider a stable first-come-first-served $M/G/k$ queue with $k\ge2$ identical servers. Arrivals form a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$, service times are iid with distribution $G$ and finite mean $1/\mu$, and the traffic intensity is $\rho=\lambda/(k\mu)<1$. Let $Q$ be the stationary number in system, $W$ the stationary waiting time, and let the full Markov state record the queue length together with residual service times of busy servers. The open problem is to find an exact representation or algorithm that computes the stationary distribution, transforms, or basic performance measures of $(Q,W)$ for arbitrary $G$ with provable finite error and complexity guarantees. The target is a theory comparable in generality to Pollaczek-Khinchine for $M/G/1$, Erlang formulas for $M/M/k$, or matrix-analytic methods for phase-type service, but without replacing $G$ by an approximation. A weaker but still meaningful resolution would prove a rigorous obstruction: for a natural input model for $G$, exact stationary performance cannot be represented or computed within a specified tractable class.
known_results: Exact formulas are known for $M/M/k$, $M/G/1$, $D/M/k$, $M/D/k$, and many phase-type or rational-transform special cases. For $M/G/2$, integral-equation and transform methods exist in special settings, and phase-type approximations convert the problem to large finite Markov chains. Tijms, van Hoorn, and Federgruen developed steady-state approximations and explicitly questioned whether computationally tractable exact methods for general $M/G/k$ steady-state probabilities are likely. Gupta, Harchol-Balter, Dai, and Zwart showed that two service-time moments are insufficient for universally accurate approximation, while Gupta and Osogami used Markov-Krein theory to obtain tight mean-waiting-time bounds under moment information. Sigman and Connor-Kendall developed exact or perfect simulation methods for stationary $M/G/c$ queues, but simulation of samples is not the same as a closed stationary characterization. The broad exact-performance problem remains open.

progress.summary: Approximations, special cases, bounds, and heavy-traffic analyses are extensive, but no general exact tractable solution is known for arbitrary service distributions.

counterexample_rationale: This is an exact-characterization problem for a continuum of service distributions. Finite examples can refute approximations but cannot by themselves prove impossibility of an exact method.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search can discover transform identities, numerical patterns, and hard service-time distributions for approximations. A resolution likely needs analytic queueing theory or a formal computational-complexity obstruction.

literature.synthesis: The obstruction in $M/G/k$ is residual-service dimensionality. In $M/G/1$, a departure or workload recursion collapses the system to one dimension. With multiple FCFS servers, the vector of residual service times matters, and arrivals see a correlated configuration of server ages. Phase-type approximations convert the problem to a finite Markov chain but can grow rapidly and do not constitute a closed-form exact solution for arbitrary $G$. Moment-based approximations are useful operationally, but impossibility results for two-moment approximations show that distributional detail can matter. The open gap is an exact representation that is both mathematically general and computationally usable.

reviewed.ref: H. C. Tijms, M. H. van Hoorn, and A. Federgruen, 'Approximations for the Steady-State Probabilities in the M/G/c Queue', Advances in Applied Probability 1981
reviewed.result: Develops approximation methods and frames the difficulty of exact steady-state computation for $M/G/c$.

reviewed.ref: Varun Gupta, Mor Harchol-Balter, J. G. Dai, and Bert Zwart, 'On the inapproximability of M/G/K: Why two moments of job size distribution are not enough', Queueing Systems 2010
reviewed.result: Shows that approximations based only on the first two service-time moments cannot be uniformly accurate.

reviewed.ref: Varun Gupta and Takanori Osogami, 'On Markov-Krein characterization of the mean waiting time in M/G/K and other queueing systems', Queueing Systems 2011
reviewed.result: Uses moment-problem methods to give tight bounds on mean waiting time under moment information.

reviewed.ref: Isaac Grosof, Ziv Scully, and Mor Harchol-Balter, 'SRPT for Multiserver Systems', arXiv 2018
reviewed.result: Illustrates recent progress on multiserver $M/G/k$ performance under specific scheduling policies and asymptotic regimes.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Look for state-space reductions based on workload vectors, symmetric residual-life measures, or transform equations. For impossibility, formalize an input model for $G$ and show exact performance encodes a hard analytic or computational problem.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A proposed formula must specialize correctly to $M/G/1$, $M/M/k$, deterministic service, and phase-type service, and it must specify how arbitrary service distributions are represented as input. A numerical method should include certified truncation or discretization error bounds; otherwise it is an approximation, not a resolution of the exact-performance problem. A claimed impossibility result must define the computational model carefully enough that it does not rule out known exact special cases or perfect-simulation algorithms.
